name: Verify

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

# A second push to the same branch makes the first run's answer worthless, so it is cancelled rather
# than left to finish. `schedule` already competes for hosted runners here (see
# check-obsidian-package-update.yml); this keeps `verify` from adding queue pressure of its own.
concurrency:
  group: verify-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      # The ROOT `npm ci` runs a `prepare` that installs husky. A runner has no commits to hook.
      # (`docs`' own `prepare` runs `astro sync` and is not affected by this.)
      HUSKY: '0'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: |
            package-lock.json
            workflow-scripts/package-lock.json
            docs/package-lock.json

      - name: Install root dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install workflow-scripts dependencies
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: ./workflow-scripts

      # `npm run lint` at the root reaches `docs/` too: that tree has no `eslint.config.mts` of its
      # own, so the nearest config to its files is the root one, which names `docs/**/*.ts` and
      # carries three dedicated override blocks. Typed linting there resolves through this install.
      #
      # It also GENERATES the types every gate below needs, which is why it carries the `id` they
      # read: `docs/package.json` has a `prepare` script running `astro sync`, and npm runs `prepare`
      # on `npm ci`. `docs/src/env.d.ts` imports `docs/.astro/types.d.ts`, which Astro generates and
      # `.gitignore` hides. Without it the root `lint` fails with 12 errors on a clean checkout -- one
      # `import-x/no-unresolved`, then 11 `no-unsafe-*` in `route-middleware.ts`, which loses its
      # types and degrades to `any`. `astro sync` is `astro build`'s implicit first step run on its
      # own (~20 s of this install's ~80): the full docs build needs ~21 GB and OOM-kills this runner
      # size (see build-pages.yml). A dedicated step here would run it a second time and leave a
      # contributor's fresh clone -- which gets it from the same install -- with nothing to copy.
      - name: Install docs dependencies
        id: prepare
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: ./docs

      # Every gate runs even after an earlier one fails, so one push reports every problem it has
      # rather than one per fix. They are skipped only when the setup above failed, where a red gate
      # would say nothing about the code.

        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.prepare.outcome == 'success' }}
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Lint
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.prepare.outcome == 'success' }}

        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.prepare.outcome == 'success' }}

        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.prepare.outcome == 'success' }}

      - name: Spellcheck
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.prepare.outcome == 'success' }}

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check
